population.label: the P frames of the 960 s cut that carry a list0 motion field

instrument: scripts/reuse_mv_gate.py --clip: warp LR_{t-d} by the list0 field of frame t, mean |LR_t - warp| over the pixels carrying a coded vector, against |LR_t - LR_{t-d}| on the same pixels
config: PyAV decode with codec_context.options flags2=+export_mvs, H.264 stream copy, 16x16/8x8 blocks, quarter-pel vectors (motion_scale 4), display order
note: the reference is the previous anchor, two display frames back: d=2 reads +2.9% median with 53% of the frames improving, while d=1 reads -16.1% with 18% improving. This is why applying the vectors to t-1 read as 'the vectors are wrong' (RU035). Note the magnitude: an earlier probe on the first 18 P frames read +9.6%, which is a prefix, not the population - over all 72 P frames the field buys 2.9%.

population.label: the reused frames of the 960 s cut that sit over the 0.1% bar under the split correction

instrument: scripts/reuse_mv_gate.py: the same warp, restricted to an 8 px border band, at the distance the gate actually holds (the reuse depth), since that is the only frame whose SR is cached
config: as RU036, band 8 px of a 1920x1080 frame (2.3% of the area), one distance per frame = its reuse depth
note: negative on 3 of the 4 failing frames (-10.4, -5.8, -32.5), +3.3 on frame 18. The field cannot be applied to the frame the gate holds and still reduce the residual in the region that fails.

population.label: the reused frames of the 960 s cut that sit over the 0.1% bar under the split correction

instrument: scripts/reuse_mv_gate.py: the same warp in the border band, but at the codec's own reference (display distance 2, the P anchor) instead of the gate's
note: even at the reference the field was coded against, the band does not improve: -16.5, -10.4, -24.4 and +1.9. So the failure is not 'the reference was wrong', which was the reading RU035 left open.

population.label: the reused frames of the 960 s cut that sit over the 0.1% bar under the split correction

instrument: a per-frame decomposition of the pixels more than 8 levels off, split into an 8 px border band and the interior, under the split correction at the served reference (jump-k)
config: rgb24, per channel, nearest-2x residual, alpha 1.35 with the flat/gradient mask, band 8 px
note: frames 18/21/22 read 9.05/9.38/16.67% of the band and 0.0000% of the interior; frame 56 reads 0.001% of the band and 0.168% of the interior. Three of the four failures are a border phenomenon, one is not.

population.label: consecutive frame pairs at the reused frames 1-56 of the 960 s cut, both frames freshly rendered

instrument: two consecutive frame pairs in the UNGATED render (both freshly rendered, no reuse involved), share of band pixels whose worst channel differs by more than 8 levels
config: w960_off.mkv, band 8 px at 4K (2.3% of the area)
run: band decomposition over the ungated render
note: at frame 22 the fresh render differs from the previous fresh render on 14.32% of the band, i.e. 0.33% of the whole frame - 3.3x the bar, before any reuse decision exists. Median over the population: 0.0888%. A verbatim reuse of any frame therefore fails the bar on that frame; the correction's job is to beat that, and it reads 0.19% instead of 0.33%, i.e. it improves the band but not to the bar.

population.label: the reused frames 9-24 of the 960 s cut, i.e. the segment where the border band starts to change

instrument: mean |LR_t - LR_{t-1}| inside the 8 px band divided by the same inside the interior, per frame
config: rgb24 1920x1080, band 4 LR px = 8 px at 4K, interior = the rest
run: band decomposition over the clip and the ungated render
note: the band is not a renderer artefact: its LR content changes 3.2x faster than the interior's (1.0 at frame 9, 9.4 at frame 22), and the SR change follows it. The band is where this clip's detail moves, and the interior is a held cel.

population.label: the reused frames of the 960 s cut, the same set the split correction is scored on

instrument: scripts/reuse_compose.py: warp the cached SR from the SERVED reference by a DIS flow gated by forward-backward consistency, add the warped residual, then the grain half on flat static blocks
config: alpha 1.35, fb tolerance 1.0 px, 1080p flow at 3-frame distance where the reuse depth is 3
note: the same four frames stay over the bar (18, 21, 22, 56) and frame 56 gets worse (0.150% -> 0.205%). Texture 1.238. So a flow from the frame the gate actually holds does not rescue the band either - the second, independent geometry route to fail on the same frames.

population.label: the reused frames 15-60 of the 960 s cut, the window the upsampling probe covered

instrument: scripts/reuse_split.py with the residual upsampled bilinearly instead of nearest-2x (NEMO upsamples the codec residual), same correction otherwise
config: alpha 1.35, blur 5, mask tau 3 / grad 5, recursive, 12 reused frames of the 960 s cut
note: bilinear reads 4 over the bar where nearest reads 3 on the same 12 frames (frame 18 crosses the bar at 0.10001%). Smoothing the correction does not fix an edge that has to MOVE; it blurs it.
